notes.title: Event review starts with care
notes.content: If a patient may still be at risk, the treating team and clinical escalation chain act first. The safety office preserves facts and coordinates learning after immediate care is addressed; it should never delay mitigation while waiting for a perfect event classification.

notes.title: Systems analysis, not automatic blame
notes.content: A useful review separates what happened, contributing conditions, barriers that worked or failed, detection, recovery and organisational factors. It does not infer negligence from an outcome or use a multi-agent benchmark to decide employment discipline.

notes.title: Corrective action strength
notes.content: Education and reminders may be appropriate but are weak when used alone. The action record should identify the hazard, responsible process owner, control type, implementation evidence, unintended consequences and an effectiveness measure with a review date.

notes.title: Patient-identification near miss
notes.content: For a wrong-chart near miss, inspect registration, wristband, device, order-entry, interface and handoff steps. Preserve minimum necessary examples inside the safety system; vendor troubleshooting should use de-identified or synthetic reproductions whenever possible.

notes.title: Vendor contribution boundary
notes.content: When a product may have contributed, Kestrel supplies a de-identified event description and affected workflow through the approved channel. The vendor investigates product behaviour. Kestrel retains the local clinical-event review and decides local mitigation.

notes.title: Safety action closure
notes.content: Closure requires more than completion. Confirm the control reached the intended units, staff can use it, process data changed in the expected direction, balancing measures did not worsen, and any residual risk has an accountable clinical owner.

notes.title: Confidentiality of safety review
notes.content: The safety record can contain patient information, staff accounts and sensitive deliberation. Share the approved learning summary with those who need it; do not copy witness statements, patient identities or speculative blame into general incident channels.

notes.title: Availability and escalation
notes.content: The safety office is not a bedside response service. Immediate concerns go to the charge nurse, attending and established escalation chain. Aisha's queue handles investigation and organisational follow-up during covered hours, with urgent duty escalation when policy requires it.
